source_inspection.method: downloaded and extracted the real npm tarball (jsora-0.3.0.tgz), independently re-verified its sha1/sha256 against the npm registry's own reported shasum, then read every src/*.js file directly with a local file-read tool -- not a web-page summary of the GitLab UI, which was tried first and found unreliable (an initial WebFetch pass over composite.js's own raw file mis-rendered the _plus function as missing its alpha-channel line; the actual downloaded file shows the alpha line is present and correct -- see composite_svg_plus below).
files: src/render.js (rendering orchestrator, svg:* -> kernel-name mapping tables)
src/blend.js (11 separable W3C blend modes as GPU.js kernels, plus 5 additional unregistered kernels: addition/subtract/grain_extract/grain_merge/divide, defined but never wired into the public API)

operation_mapping_table_render_js.default_else_branch: normal blend, implicit svg:src-over -- matches the registry's own DEFAULT_COMPOSITE_OP
operation_mapping_table_render_js.coverage_vs_COMPOSITE_OP_REGISTRY: 10 + 4 + 5 + 1(default) = 20 of 20 registry entries have an attempted mapping. This is a genuine, source-verified claim, not an inference from the README's unenumerated 'all blend modes' text.

formula_analysis_before_empirical_testin.method: hand-derived algebraic comparison against composite_oracle.py's own already-independently-derived W3C/Porter-Duff formulas, to predict which operations are likely to match empirically and which are not, BEFORE running any browser execution -- not a substitute for the actual pixel-level spike, which follows.
formula_analysis_before_empirical_testin.svg:plus (composite.js, _plus): oa = min(ua+la, 1.0); or/og/ob = min((ua*ur)+(la*lr), 1.0) -- this is the textbook Porter-Duff Lighter formula in premultiplied space (Fa=Fb=1, clamped), matching composite_oracle.py's own porter_duff_coeffs('Lighter', ...) == (1.0, 1.0) exactly. Predicted: MATCH, pending the out-of-bounds caveat below.
formula_analysis_before_empirical_testin.svg:dst-in / svg:dst-out / svg:src-atop: All 4 algebraically match composite_oracle.py's own Porter & Duff (1984) coefficients exactly when hand-expanded. Predicted: MATCH for in-bounds pixels.
formula_analysis_before_empirical_testin.out_of_bounds_bug_class_shared_with_form: All 5 Porter-Duff kernels in composite.js use the identical structural pattern: 'if (i>=0 && i<sourceWidth && j>=0 && j<sourceHeight) { <formula> } else { this.color(lr,lg,lb,la); }' -- i.e. OUTSIDE the source layer's own declared bounds, the destination is always left UNCHANGED, for every one of the 5 operators including dst_in and dst_atop. This is the exact same bug class independently found and fixed in format-factory's own render.py this session (Destination In/Atop require the destination to be CLEARED outside source bounds, not left unchanged, since their own Fb=alpha_s=0 there). PREDICTION, not yet confirmed empirically: if the existing discriminating fixture (composite_matrix.py PORTER_DUFF_SCENES, which places source layer smaller than the canvas specifically to exercise a destination-only sample point) is reused unmodified, jsora's dst_in and dst_atop are likely to MISMATCH at the destination-only sample point, for the same root cause already diagnosed once this session -- not a fixture problem, a real, disclosable jsora defect if confirmed.
formula_analysis_before_empirical_testin.svg:overlay (blend.js, _overlay): Hand-expanded jsora's own branch-on-backdrop formula and confirmed it is algebraically identical to composite_oracle.py's own _overlay(cb,cs) = _hard_light(cs,cb) definition (both reduce to the same 2 branches). Predicted: MATCH -- unlike GIMP 2.10's own confirmed-non-conformant Overlay (delta=6).
formula_analysis_before_empirical_testin.svg:soft-light (blend.js, _soft_light): Hand-expanded jsora's own core formula (ignoring an alpha==0 edge-case fallback term that never fires against this session's own always-opaque-backdrop discriminating fixture) and found it matches the well-known 'Pegtop' soft-light approximation ((1-2*Cs)*Cb^2 + 2*Cs*Cb), NOT the W3C spec's own literal piecewise formula (which composite_oracle.py implements exactly, per the spec text). Predicted: MEASURABLE MISMATCH for at least some inputs -- a real, different-but-not-identical divergence from the W3C spec, distinct from (not proof of relation to) GIMP's own non-conformance.
formula_analysis_before_empirical_testin.svg:hue / svg:saturation / svg:color / s: Structurally implement the correct SetLum/SetSat/ClipColor algorithm shape from the W3C spec, but use luma coefficients (0.299, 0.587, 0.114 -- ITU-R BT.601/NTSC) that differ from the W3C Compositing spec's own literal coefficients (0.3, 0.59, 0.11), which composite_oracle.py implements exactly. Predicted: MEASURABLE MISMATCH -- close but not bit-identical, a real, different-but-not-identical divergence from the W3C spec, again distinct from GIMP's own non-conformance (GIMP's own deltas for these 4 operations ranged 8-29/255; jsora's expected delta from a 0.001-0.023 luma-coefficient difference is likely much smaller but still nonzero for saturated colors).

source_inspection.rendering_pipeline: render.js's own render_to_canvas() requires a real WebGL2 context (canvas.getContext('webgl2', {premultipliedAlpha:false})) to construct the gpu.js GPU instance every kernel runs through -- there is no Canvas2D/CPU-only fallback path in this version. This is a genuine environment requirement for the execution spike (headless Chromium must expose functioning WebGL2, e.g. via SwiftShader software rendering, not merely a DOM), not yet verified working in this project's own Docker environment.
source_inspection.write_path: index.js's own save() builds a real ZIP via JSZip (mimetype + stack.xml + layer/thumbnail/mergedimage members) -- independently verified via direct grep of the downloaded source, not inferred from the README.
source_inspection.read_path: index.js's own load path uses JSZip.loadAsync + zip.file('stack.xml').async('string') -- independently verified, a real, separate parse path from format-factory's own codec/stack_xml.py.

lineage_independence_check.shares_code_with_format_factory: No -- different language (JavaScript vs Python), different runtime (browser/WebGL vs CPU), no import or reference to format_factory anywhere in the downloaded source (grepped).
lineage_independence_check.shares_code_with_gimp_or_krita_or_mypain: No evidence found -- jsora's own compositor is GPU.js-kernel-based JavaScript, structurally and technologically unrelated to GIMP's C/GEGL pipeline or Krita's C++/Qt pipeline. No shared authorship, dependency, or vendored code identified.
lineage_independence_check.other_inklab_packages: pyora (github/gitlab: inklabapp/pyora) is a separate, PURE PYTHON package under the same InkLab organization/author. Different language from jsora (Python vs JavaScript/WebGL), so it cannot share jsora's own GPU.js-kernel compositor implementation even in principle. pyora is NOT being counted as a producer in this audit -- noted here only to answer the directive's own explicit lineage-sharing question, not because it is in use.
lineage_independence_check.verdict: No evidence of shared implementation code with format-factory, GIMP, Krita, or MyPaint. Same-author (InkLab) sibling package (pyora) exists but is a different language/runtime and is not being counted.
